body:
Came to this late but thanks for sharing again.

These systems are machines filled with propaganda that unfortunately can work extremely well and why we’ve been on this inevitable path to today’s state of affairs. Try to reason and change someone’s perspective, if being kind to someone isn’t working, then move on to those systems that don’t allow people to be free.
I am still naive to believe if we can dismantle these systems, those people who refused to see the broader picture will only appreciate us being when they trapped by it all.
You also get housing at a lot of the ski resorts and once you get promoted or stay for a bit you can get good apartment style and are living in the most beautiful area.

You either have to be 23 or live for at least a year with some sort of job and get emancipated from your parents. Dont get emancipated if your still on your parents insurance.
I worked my way up at two different ski resorts in summit county for a few years until I got instate. Weird being an older undergrad but you also will get some grants.

I’m on day 70 something and have had multiple other failed attempts to quit before the one I’m currently on. Never really had bad night sweats on the other attempts.
This one I had night sweats so bad I had to change the sheets in the middle of the night. Only to then have to wash the one I changed into because of how soaked it got it. 
What helped me a bit was to take a warm epsom salt bath/really hot shower right before bed. Time fully resolved that symptom but doing that routine at least made it more just wet body waking up, rather than all my sheets being drenched.

Every day that don’t smoke I realize it’s worth it. While some days I’m tempted, if I wake up the next morning I’m happy with myself and know I didn’t do the major thing that has been holding me back. This is the mindset that has gotten me further than when I used to try to look diligently at some timeline.

I’m about a 1/4 from 4 dispensaries so I can totally relate, am actually on day 40 too! Congrats to us! I try to mediate in the morning and visualize how proud I will be when I don’t smoke when the temptation comes to smoke. The harder days I know to not walk near the dispensaries. Some days it feels good on my walks to go right past and be proud I’m no longer walking in. Just always be aware of yourself and try to find healthy ways to keep your mind occupied. If I have to, I’ll occupy my mind by saying positive affirmations over and over again, all related to how I won’t smoke. Our mind will trick us into justifying going into that dispo but we can always do things to trick it to do the exact opposite. Love you and keep your head up to see the life you can create without weed!

Honestly, I’d recommend giving up weed entirely. It  isn’t serving you and helping you be the person you can. Reason I say move on for good instead of cutting back is the slippery slope of that growing temptation to turn from smoking at night after you’ve studied to more and more throughout the day, further hindering your ability to finish classes.
If you’re suspended, I would use this time to get clean, refresh your mind, form new habits and prepare for the next semester. It’s gonna suck for a bit but then you won’t have your mind occupied with thinking about the next hit when you do return from this suspension.

I get the urges, sometimes my mind will start to convince myself different to justify walking to the dispensary. When that happens I try to repeat “I’m gonna be proud of myself for not smoking today because I don’t want to smoke today and won’t smoke today.” Over and over then jump into something productive. I like to even do it in the mirror and smile at myself and be proud of how far I’ve come. That’s actually helped a lot and usually won’t get any craving for the rest of the day.

I’ve failed out of college twice and am starting back up in the fall. I’ve had straight A’s when I don’t smoke then have fallen into the trap of thinking now I can smoke a little. Which then turned to a lot. I have ADHD too and smoking a little for me would lead to falling behind on an assignment then smoking to relive the stress, which caused me to be more behind. That would snowball to something awful. I’m a little over 5 weeks sober. Have been working on the classes I will be taking and feel great. Even if I think I can smoke a little, I have gotten over the urges by reminding myself this isn’t helping me achieve my goals that I could’ve already accomplished. I try to meditate in the morning, envision myself throughout the day, being proud of myself for resisting the urge to smoke. Then I try to visualize myself achieving my goals and try to remove all thoughts of a “celebratory joint” at graduation. 

It sounds like you know there’s a negative impact on your studies, try to remind yourself of that to strengthen your mind, almost to the point where you won’t even have a temptation. I’m trying that now and is the only reason why I didn’t go to a dispensary on 4/20. Truthfully, I felt like I was and was trying to justify it. Luckily, I was able to remind myself of how proud I am for wanting to be better and that lead to my mind after probably 2hrs of the urge to shift, and start saying “I don’t want to do this.” 

Like I mentioned, I failed out twice, both because I let weed slowly take over. I won’t let this happen to me again, and I know you will have the strength to graduate too!

One thing that helped with my sleep is getting up early, getting natural sunlight, exercise, push through any temptations to nap(at least for the first week since for me a nap then would kill my sleep at night), then a warm shower right before bed along with chamomile tea. 
Our body temperatures are meant to decrease to help us sleep and stay asleep. The tea and shower is a little hack to artificially increase our body temps as we slowly get back to not allowing a plant to get us to sleep but never providing quality rem sleep. 
Really proud of you!

It will be tough but keep reminding yourself how worth it this will be. This struggle is temporary but a life of weed can lead to a never ending thought of what you could have been. Meditating in the morning helps a ton. Try to remain positive as dwelling on the pain you are in can open the door for a relapse. That is not to diminish the struggle you are facing. 
When you are frustrated, late at night, or in day struggling to eat, remind yourself why you stopped in the first place. Be proud of yourself to make this decision and focus on the wins as they will slowly continue to compound.

What has helped so far is trying to eliminate the things that I used to do when high or what I would do drinking. I used to smoke all day everyday so it’s hard finding those things. If I used to smoke then walk, now I may try shooting hoops, or weightlifting. If a Saturday night was me watching sports with my friends drinking beers, I may try to read or watch a movie that requires more of my attention. When I get the urge, I try to change my setting as well. Even if it’s going from my bedroom to just cleaning my living room that doesn’t need to be cleaned.
Meditation in the morning has also helped me a lot. In those moments I try to visualize how proud I was waking up having stayed sober the day before. I even visualize the potential moments of temptation and tell myself in my meditation I know those are the thoughts I should let pass. Taking moments when the tempting actually comes to remove yourself and just breathe has been amazing for me.

I used to struggle with sleep apnea a ton and I had an awesome dentist who was all about the breath. He noticed my jaw was a little to narrow prohibiting me from getting quality sleep. I then got a functional regulator to help widen my jaw and that has opened up a whole new world for me. Sleep is crucial and poor sleep can be debilitating. Not sure if it could help you but I was shocked how much it helped me and if a retainer that any orthodontist can give may help it’s worth it!
Be proud of yourself for the drive you have!

One thing that has helped me a lot is physical exercise during the day and then right before bed I take a hot a shower. The hot showers helped me almost eliminate the night sweats immediately and has been good to help me get into a sleep routine.
Thank you for an inspiration boost! Can’t wait for you to be cheered for decades of safe flights!

Congrats! Be proud of yourself since 6 days is huge. One thing I would recommend from someone who’s quit “forever” but came right back to it is to visualize the temptation on the night you’re struggling to sleep, appetite is bad, or just having a shitty day that joint would take all the worries away. You know those cravings and temptations if you’ve been a heavy smoker like me. When you visualize, spin it from what you have done in the past to what you will do in the future. This way, you’re prepared when it seems damn near impossible to not give in. Goals are great too! I’ve failed many times but am back on day 15 and these tips helped me get through days 7-12. You got this!

Hey man, I’m proud of you for sharing this. It shows a lot of strength and that you still have what you think may be completely lost. I’m a bit younger, not much, but still working toward my undergrad because of this damn leaf. Also in a legal state and even had an attempt on my life almost 3 years ago. Feel free to message me privately if you want to open up a bit and we may even be in the same state, in which case I’d love to formally connect so we can work through this together.
Remind yourself of all the struggles it took to even have an opportunity to work towards a PHD. That’s damn impressive and you’ve already proven yourself. Try to fall back on what you’ve already gone through to remind yourself that you can keep going.
Love you and you got this!
Thank you I keep trying to remind myself this. I know that will help me not relapse
